scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A report they cannot reach
anything outside their own VLAN. Internal pings to other Office-A
data PCs still work, but Internet access and reaching Office B
services hang. Investigate.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r1 stopped sending OSPF hellos and LSAs. CSW1/CSW2
  aged out r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) and the default route r1
  originated via `default-information originate`. Office-A
  internal traffic still works because DSWs route locally,
  but anything beyond the OSPF backbone (Internet, Office B
  via core) has no next hop and is dropped.
Localization: r1
Root cause: OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) not running on r1
Fix: restart frr on r1 — `/etc/init.d/frr restart`

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on **r1**: its FRR routing daemon has no OSPF configuration whatsoever. The running-config contains only a loopback interface assignment (`10.0.0.76/32`) and nothing else — no `router ospf` block, no `default-information originate`, and no OSPF-enabled interfaces.

Because r1 is not running OSPF, it never forms adjacencies with csw1 (WAN link eth0, 10.0.0.32/30) or csw2 (WAN link eth1, 10.0.0.36/30). This was confirmed directly: neither csw1 nor csw2 lists r1 as an OSPF neighbor. r1's own routing table shows only its static kernel default route (`0.0.0.0/0 via 203.0.113.1 eth2`) and connected prefixes — no OSPF routes at all, meaning r1 cannot even reach internal hosts by their subnet addresses.

The consequence propagates down the entire OSPF domain: csw1 and csw2 have no default route, and so neither do dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, or dswb2. When PC1 sends any packet to a destination outside the 10.x.x.x internal space (e.g., 8.8.8.8), it is forwarded to its gateway dswa1 (10.1.0.1 on br0.10), which immediately returns ICMP Network Unreachable (!N at hop 1 in traceroute) because it holds no `0.0.0.0/0` route. Internal Office-B hosts (10.3.0.0/24, 10.5.0.0/24) remain reachable because their prefixes are fully distributed by OSPF among the switching layer.

**Root cause:** r1's OSPF process was never configured (or was removed), so the WAN default route is stranded on r1 and never injected into the campus OSPF domain.

**Fix:** Add OSPF to r1 — enable `router ospf` with `ospf router-id 10.0.0.76`, add `ip ospf area 0` to eth0 and eth1 (the csw1/csw2 uplinks), and add `default-information originate always` so that r1's static default route is redistributed as an OSPF type-5 external LSA. This will give every downstream switch a default route pointing via r1, restoring Internet access.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names r1 as the device with the fault and describes its missing OSPF configuration.
The report explicitly identifies r1's OSPF/ospfd (FRR OSPF daemon and missing OSPF configuration) as the faulty component.

The report clearly explains the mechanism: ospfd absent on r1 -> no OSPF adjacencies/LSAs -> CSWs age out r1's loopback and default route -> downstream devices lack a default route and Internet-bound traffic is dropped.

The agent recommends adding OSPF config on r1 rather than performing the expected fix of restarting the FRR daemon (/etc/init.d/frr restart), so the proposed remediation does not match the required action.

The agent's investigation log contains multiple specific observations (no r1 OSPF adjacency on neighbors, r1 routing table lacking OSPF routes, dswa1 lacking a default route and returning !N, internal prefixes reachable) that directly support the conclusion that r1 is not participating in OSPF and therefore not injecting the default. The reasoning chain from those observations to the root cause and fix is logical and complete with only minor unshown but implied outputs.
